summary: Module covers the three headline exposures (monlist / mode-6 readvar / clock-skew) plus mode-7 peer_list, but leaves the majority of mode-6 opcodes, most mode-7 request codes, and every post-2014 ntpd CVE untouched. Biggest gap is that monlist is detected as a *volume* only — the ~600 client IPs it returns are never parsed, so the free host-discovery use-case is thrown away. Version banner is fetched via readvar but never cross-checked against vulnerable ranges (CVE-2014-9293/95, 2016-7431/34, 2018-7182, 2020-11868/13817, 2023-266xx). No auth-mode probing (Autokey RFC 5906, symmetric-key MAC), no NTS-KE (RFC 8915) awareness, no KoD interpretation.
existing_capabilities: RFC 5905 mode-3 client packet + reachability + stratum/version/mode decode
Clock-skew measurement against midpoint of send/recv, Kerberos 5-min tolerance test (MS-KILE)
Refid decode (stratum-1 ASCII clock id vs stratum-2+ IPv4)
RFC 1305 App. B mode-6 READVAR (opcode 2, assoc=0) with ASCII k=v parsing
ntpd version extraction from version= plus processor/system/leap/stratum sysinfo
Mode-7 REQ_MON_GETLIST_1 (code 42) — CVE-2013-5211 detect + amplification ratio
Finding for peer_list suppressed when monlist already fires (dedupe)

missing_capabilities.name: monlist entry parsing → known_hosts / relay_targets feed
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: ntpd mode-7 MON_GETLIST_1 (info_monitor_1 struct: firsttime, lasttime, restr, count, addr, daddr, flags, port, mode, version)
missing_capabilities.description: Response volume is measured but the payload is discarded. Each entry carries client IPv4 (and daddr = local interface), port, mode, count and lastseen. These IPs are the whole point of the finding on an internal engagement — should be extracted, deduped, and fed to hostnames/hosts as newly-discovered assets and to relay_targets (clients that talk to a DC are frequently DC-adjacent). Currently zero cross-service wire.

missing_capabilities.name: peer_list entry parsing → known_hosts / relay_targets feed
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: ntpd mode-7 REQ_PEER_LIST info_peer_list (srcadr, srcport, hmode, flags)
missing_capabilities.description: peer_list is flagged as present, but the peer IPs (upstream time sources, often internal appliances or DCs) are never extracted. Same wire gap as monlist.

missing_capabilities.name: ntpd version → CVE cross-check
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: N/A — post-extraction gate
missing_capabilities.description: ntpd_version is captured but never compared to known-vulnerable ranges: <4.2.8 (2014-9293/9294/9295 auth-key/crypto_recv BO), 4.2.8p8- (2016-1548 xleave, 2016-7431 zero-origin bypass, 2016-7434 mrulist NULL deref), 4.2.8p11- (2018-7182/7183/7184/7185), 4.2.8p14- (2020-11868/13817/15025 off-path spoof + amplification), and 4.2.8p18/ntpsec-1.2.2- (2023-26551..26555). Trivial add on top of existing parse.

missing_capabilities.name: mrulist (mode-6 CTL_OP_REQ_NONCE + read_mru)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: ntpq mrulist — opcode 12 REQ_NONCE then opcode 10 with 'nonce=..., frags=32' as data; ntpd 4.2.7+
missing_capabilities.description: monlist replacement in ntpd ≥4.2.7. Modern hardened boxes disable monitor but still answer mrulist to unauthed queriers — same last-N-clients disclosure as CVE-2013-5211. Not probed at all; module misses every 4.2.7+ deployment.

missing_capabilities.name: REQ_GET_RESTRICT (mode-7 code 16)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: ntpd request.h REQ_GET_RESTRICT / info_restrict
missing_capabilities.description: Dumps the ACL table (addr, mask, flags, count). Reveals which subnets are trusted for mode 6/7/config, exposing management networks and any wildcard restrict entries. Cheap one-datagram probe; also useful amplification vector.

missing_capabilities.name: CTL_OP_READSTAT (mode-6 opcode 1) + per-assoc READVAR walk
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 1305 App. B opcode 1 (read status) returns 16-bit assoc IDs + peer status
missing_capabilities.description: READVAR assoc=0 (already implemented) only gives system vars. Opcode 1 returns the full association list; iterating READVAR against each assoc id yields per-peer srcadr, srcport, hmode, hpoll, refid, reach, stratum, jitter — full topology with authoritative peer IPs and their reach state. Standard ntpq -p pipeline.

missing_capabilities.name: CTL_OP_READ_CLOCK (mode-6 opcode 5)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 1305 App. B opcode 5 with a clock assoc id
missing_capabilities.description: Reference-clock vars (device path, GPS/PPS/PTP hardware id, driver name). On appliances this fingerprints the hardware (GPS antenna, PTP grandmaster, refclock driver version) — separate exposure from readvar.

missing_capabilities.name: REQ_SYS_INFO / REQ_SYS_STATS / REQ_IO_STATS / REQ_MEM_STATS / REQ_TIMER_STATS (mode-7 codes 4/6/7/8/10)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: ntpd request.h
missing_capabilities.description: Free operational disclosure — precision, refid, syspeer, packet counters, memory table sizes, timer overrun. Reveals daemon activity level and version-specific field layouts (fingerprinting).

missing_capabilities.name: REQ_IF_STATS (mode-7 code 44)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: ntpd request.h REQ_IF_STATS info_if_stats
missing_capabilities.description: Lists every bound interface with its IPv4/IPv6 address and index — enumerates multi-homed hosts (jump boxes, dual-NIC firewalls, management VLANs). Directly feeds hostnames/hosts across networks recce hasn't scanned yet.

missing_capabilities.name: Autokey (mode-3 with extension field) detection
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 5906 (deprecated, cryptographically broken 2019+)
missing_capabilities.description: No probe for Autokey. `crypto` field in readvar or extension-field capability in mode-3 response identifies servers with Autokey enabled — a finding on its own (deprecated + broken IFF/GQ/MV identity schemes, key-exchange DoS).

missing_capabilities.name: Symmetric-key MAC probe (crypto-NAK path)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 5905 §7.5 + CVE-2015-7871 crypto-NAK auth bypass ('NAK to the Future')
missing_capabilities.description: Send a mode-3 with a bogus MAC/key-id: pre-4.2.8p4 ntpd honours it as an authenticated peer (CVE-2015-7871). Also detects whether symmetric-key auth is enabled at all (MD5-only vs SHA1/AES-128-CMAC). No probe today.

missing_capabilities.name: CVE-2016-7431 zero-origin timestamp spoof
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 5905 §8 origin timestamp; ntpd <4.2.8p9
missing_capabilities.description: Send a mode-4 with origin=0: vulnerable ntpd accepts it and updates state, enabling off-path time-shift. Detectable by observing state change on a follow-up readvar (reftime advances) after a zero-origin injection.

missing_capabilities.name: CVE-2020-13817 off-path origin-timestamp leak
missing_capabilities.description: Origin timestamp derived from predictable transmit — allows off-path attackers to guess and desync. Version-gated detection (piggybacks on the CVE cross-check gap above but is a distinct primitive).

missing_capabilities.name: CVE-2016-1550 sysvar timing side channel
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: ntpd <4.2.8p7 authenticate() timing
missing_capabilities.description: Timing oracle on MAC verification. Not runtime-detected today.

missing_capabilities.name: Kiss-of-Death (KoD) interpretation on stratum=0
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 5905 §7.4 — refid 4-char codes: DENY, RATE, RSTR, INIT, STEP, MCST, ACST, AUTH, AUTO, CRYP, NKEY, NTSN
missing_capabilities.description: When pkt[1]=0 the refid is an ASCII KoD code, not an IP. Current code branches on stratum==1 for ASCII but not stratum==0. DENY/RSTR tells the tester which restrict flag hit; AUTH/CRYP/NKEY/NTSN reveals authentication posture. Never surfaced.

missing_capabilities.name: Refid IPv6 hash detect (RFC 5905 §7.3)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 5905 §7.3 — stratum≥2 refid = MD5 hash of source when IPv6
missing_capabilities.description: Non-routable-looking 4 bytes get emitted as bogus IPv4 dotted-quad. Should be recognised and flagged as IPv6 upstream (still a topology signal, but not a directly usable IP).

missing_capabilities.name: Refid IP → known_hosts / relay_targets feed
missing_capabilities.description: Stratum-2+ refid is the upstream server's IPv4 — on a corporate LAN this is nearly always the DC or the internal time appliance. Currently only rendered into the finding text; not fed to hostnames/relay_targets/dc_candidates.

missing_capabilities.name: Hostname / OS extraction from readvar → known_hostnames + host.notes
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: ntpq readvar system= often contains kernel version 'Linux/3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64' plus 'hostname' var on some builds
missing_capabilities.description: sysinfo dict is stored on the probe result and rendered into the mode-6 finding but never fed to the shared host fingerprint / hostname stores. Duplicate work for every other module doing OS discovery.

missing_capabilities.name: Chrony vs ntpd vs openntpd vs w32time fingerprinting
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: chrony refuses mode-6/7 by default (cmdmon on 323/udp), openntpd never answers mode-6/7, Windows w32time returns stratum-typed refid strings ('LOCL' / DC08)
missing_capabilities.description: Module conflates 'no monlist' with 'hardened ntpd'. Distinguishing chrony/openntpd/w32time drives exploit selection (chrony has cmdmon CVEs, w32time drives Kerberos infrastructure identification).

missing_capabilities.name: Chrony cmdmon (323/udp) probe
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: chrony cmdmon protocol; CVE-2020-14367 (chronyd pidfile), CVE-2023-32617 chronyc auth
missing_capabilities.description: recce only touches 123/udp. When 323/udp is open chrony exposes SYSTEMSTATS/TRACKING/SOURCES — analogue of monlist for chrony. Currently entirely absent.

missing_capabilities.name: NTS-KE (4460/tcp) detection
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 8915 Network Time Security key establishment
missing_capabilities.description: Positive-control: NTS deployed is a good posture signal and negates several off-path CVEs. Currently no awareness — cannot even distinguish NTS-protected from bare NTP.

missing_capabilities.name: Broadcast/multicast responder detection (224.0.1.1 / mode 5)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 5905 §3 broadcast mode 5
missing_capabilities.description: Passive listen for broadcast/multicast NTP identifies servers advertising themselves + reveals additional clients accepting broadcasts (spoof-target inventory).

missing_capabilities.name: REQ_AUTHINFO / REQ_TRUSTKEY presence (mode-7 codes 28/26)
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: ntpd request.h — REQ_AUTHINFO returns numkeys, numfreekeys, keylookups, keynotfound, encryptions, decryptions, expired, uncached
missing_capabilities.description: Discloses whether authentication is even configured on the server and its usage counters. Distinguishes 'no MAC configured' from 'MAC required but you didn't send one'.

missing_capabilities.name: CVE-2014-9293/9294/9295 vulnerable-version detection
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: ntpd <4.2.8: default trusted key + weak key gen + crypto_recv/ctl_putdata/configure stack overflows (unauthenticated RCE with autokey)
missing_capabilities.description: Version already parsed — a single semver compare fires a critical finding on unauthed-RCE-eligible daemons. Currently absent.

missing_capabilities.name: CVE-2016-7434 unauth mrulist NULL-deref DoS
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: ntpd <4.2.8p9 read_mru_list()
missing_capabilities.description: Malformed mrulist request crashes ntpd. Detectable as a version gate; active PoC is intrusive so gate behind --active-exploit.

missing_capabilities.name: CVE-2018-7182 ctl_getitem OOB read
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: ntpd <4.2.8p11 mode-6 ctl_getitem
missing_capabilities.description: Version-gated finding on the same readvar path recce already speaks.

missing_capabilities.name: Amplification classification for reflection register
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: US-CERT TA14-013A
missing_capabilities.description: Amplification ratio is measured but never surfaced to a cross-service 'amplifier register' (should join DNS ANY, memcached, SSDP, chargen amplifier inventory feeding external-exposure findings).

missing_capabilities.name: REQ_GET_KERNEL (mode-7 code 38) kernel PLL disclosure
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: ntpd request.h info_kernel
missing_capabilities.description: Discloses kernel PLL parameters (offset, freq, jitter, stability) — precise fingerprint of kernel time-adj implementation.

cross_service_wire_gaps: monlist client IPs (up to ~600) never parsed → hostnames/relay_targets/dc_adjacent — largest missed value in the module
peer_list peer IPs never parsed → hostnames/relay_targets (upstream time source = internal appliance/DC)
Stratum-2+ refid IP never fed to hostnames/relay_targets/dc_candidates (typically the DC on a corporate LAN)
sysinfo (system=/processor=/version=) captured but not fed to shared host fingerprint / known_hostnames — every other module re-derives OS
REQ_IF_STATS interface list would reveal multi-homed hosts on unscanned networks, not probed
Amplification ratio not registered with a shared amplifier/external-exposure ledger
priority_gaps: P0: parse monlist entries → feed client IPs to hostnames/relay_targets (the whole point of CVE-2013-5211 on an internal engagement is being thrown away)
P0: version-based CVE gate — 2014-9293/95 (unauth RCE-class), 2015-7871 (NAK-to-the-Future), 2016-7431/34, 2018-7182, 2020-11868/13817, 2023-266xx — trivial add on top of already-parsed ntpd_version
P1: mrulist (mode-6 REQ_NONCE + read_mru) — same disclosure as monlist for ntpd ≥4.2.7, currently 0% coverage of modern hardened boxes
P1: parse peer_list + stratum-2+ refid → hostnames/relay_targets — upstream IPs are DC/appliance candidates
P1: REQ_GET_RESTRICT (mode-7 code 16) — dumps ACL table, reveals trusted management subnets
P1: CTL_OP_READSTAT + per-assoc READVAR walk — full ntpq -p equivalent, authoritative peer topology
P2: Autokey (RFC 5906) + symmetric-MAC auth-mode probe (CVE-2015-7871 NAK bypass on <4.2.8p4)
P2: REQ_IF_STATS (mode-7 code 44) — bound-interface enumeration on multi-homed hosts
P2: KoD refid decoding on stratum=0 (DENY/RSTR/AUTH/NTSN — tells the tester exactly which control fired)
P3: chrony cmdmon (323/udp) probe + chrony/openntpd/w32time fingerprint disambiguation
P3: REQ_SYS_INFO / REQ_AUTHINFO / REQ_GET_KERNEL / READ_CLOCK opcodes for supplementary disclosure
P3: NTS-KE (4460/tcp) awareness for posture control
notes: Test suite is protocol-faithful (fixtures built from raw struct, not the encoder under test) — good foundation. Additions should follow the same discipline: wire-format fixtures, per-opcode fake responder branches. The FakeNtpd already dispatches by mode/req and can be extended with mrulist, get_restrict, readstat, if_stats without restructuring.
